q1: WITH S AS (SELECT ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR FROM TAKES NATURAL JOIN SECTION GROUP BY ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT TIME_SLOT_ID) > 4) SELECT DISTINCT ID, NAME FROM S NATURAL JOIN STUDENT
q2: WITH S AS (SELECT ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR FROM TAKES NATURAL JOIN SECTION GROUP BY ID, TIME_SLOT_ID, YEAR HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT TIME_SLOT_ID) > 5) SELECT DISTINCT ID, NAME FROM S NATURAL JOIN STUDENT

counterexample: INSERT INTO SECTION (COURSE_ID, SEC_ID, YEAR, BUILDING, ROOM_NUMBER, TIME_SLOT_ID) VALUES (1, 1, 2021, 'Building A', 101, 1), (1, 2, 2021, 'Building A', 102, 2), (1, 3, 2021, 'Building A', 103, 3), (1, 4, 2021, 'Building A', 104, 4), (1, 5, 2021, 'Building A', 105, 5); INSERT INTO TAKES (ID, COURSE_ID, SEC_ID, YEAR, GRADE) SELECT 1, 1, 1, 2021, NULL UNION ALL SELECT 1, 1, 2, 2021, NULL UNION ALL SELECT 1, 1, 3, 2021, NULL UNION ALL SELECT 1, 1, 4, 2021, NULL UNION ALL SELECT 1, 1, 5, 2021, NULL; INSERT INTO STUDENT (ID, NAME, DEPT_NAME, TOT_CRED) VALUES (1, 'Student1', 'CS', 100);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because the condition in the HAVING clause of the common table expression (CTE) S is different. Q1 checks for COUNT(DISTINCT TIME_SLOT_ID) > 4, while Q2 checks for COUNT(DISTINCT TIME_SLOT_ID) > 5. This difference in the threshold will result in different sets of IDs being selected in the final SELECT statement.
counterexample_dsp: The difference in the threshold condition will cause Q1 and Q2 to return different results. A counterexample can be created by inserting a student who has taken 5 different time slots in a course, which will be included in Q2's result but not in Q1's result.
